backbone: Reduce Hodge monomials on CM abelian varieties to balanced tensors on auxiliary CM factors, connect type lists by algebraic four-factor switches (via theta one-forms on ball quotients), assemble and descend.
quote: For higher codimension, we first replace a Hodge monomial by a tensor on auxiliary CM factors. We then connect its two lists of types by four-factor switches and compose the resulting algebraic tensors.

backbone: Relative Iitaka reduction gives an exact comparison of pluricanonical sections with an adjoint pair (W,T,M) carrying a Hodge line; adjoint positivity of that line plus log-general-type addition yields the inequality.
quote: Section~\ref{application:section} then returns once to the original fibration, applies the addition principle to $(W,T,M)$, and derives the ordinary, logarithmic, characteristic-zero, and core consequences.

backbone: Prove by dimension induction a stronger birational statement (semiample positive part plus effective negative part) using analytic MMP programs, boundary generation along dlt strata and descent along fibrations.
quote: The argument passes through a stronger birational statement: every pseudo-effective smooth log adjoint has a semiample positive part and an effective rational fixed divisor equal to its analytic divisorial negative part. This form both supports the induction

backbone: Assuming failure (nef dimension three), reduce to a terminal model and build a prepared boundary cycle whose existence is forbidden by the companion cycle-obstruction theorem.
quote: To prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, it suffices to rule out the following data: an uncountable algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>3$, a terminal $\Q$-factorial projective threefold $X$, an lc pair $(X,B)$

backbone: Simultaneous dimension induction: reduce full nef dimension to klt Calabi-Yau pairs, force bigness of M via jets and Frobenius comparison, then descend positive parts along the nef reduction.
quote: We prove the following two assertions together, by induction on $n$.

backbone: Induction on dimension: stable degeneration to a K-polystable cone; stabilizer and jet/semigroup estimates force a Gorenstein cone of small embedding dimension; Liu's lci theorem gives bound and equality.
quote: Starting from the known cases in dimensions two and three and the fourfold companion, we argue by induction.

backbone: If generation fails, an attained exponential minimization yields a center; positive-dimensional centers die by first-variation versus Brunn-Minkowski contradiction; isolated centers lift sections by vanishing.
quote: Second, a first variation in directions tangent to a positive-dimensional center gives an upper bound for a weighted moment of initial exponents. A uniform restriction-space estimate and Brunn--Minkowski give a contradictory lower bound.

backbone: Assume a violating curve; specialize points onto a chosen plane curve to get a normal polynomial, collide points, and show the limiting interpolation matrix has full rank.
quote: Suppose that $d\le km$ and $\mathsf U_r(d,m)$ holds. We choose the marked points to exclude normal polynomials of fiber degree below $m$, and the displacements to exclude fiber degree $m$.

backbone: Equivariant obstruction theory on determinant-fixed Quot schemes; virtual localization gives a Chow relation whose diagonal coefficient is nonzero (lattice-rank and K^2=9 cases), forcing CH_0 = Z.
quote: We construct its obstruction theory and the compatible fixed theory using a derived determinant fiber normalized at a point of $X$ (Sections~\ref{sec:derived} and~\ref{sec:fixed}).

backbone: Polarized degeneration keeping the isotropic class; torus-scale metric limits give a special Lagrangian torus; hyperkahler rotation gives a semiample point; deformation returns semiampleness to X.
quote: Soldatenkov and Verbitsky show that a fixed isotropic class is semiample at every nef point of its deformation component as soon as it is semiample at one point~\cite[Theorem~3.7(v)]{SV}.

backbone: A local criterion (two complete holomorphic directions) feeds spray-gluing to polydisc and convex approximation; complete directions on every K3 are built via symplectic sewing, degenerations and period dynamics.
quote: Our proof uses local chart sprays and splitting arguments in this tradition, with the uniform estimates needed for the strip and convex-face constructions made explicit.

backbone: Construct a common lowering operator f with [[f,e],e]=-2e on full fixed-determinant cohomology, verify Lefschetz properties for both perverse and weight filtrations, and apply a linear-algebra two-filtration comparison criterion.
quote: We then give the linear-algebra argument that will compare the filtrations once a common lowering operator has been constructed.

backbone: Abelianize the Coulomb algebra with minuscule generators, test relations by stable pairs for a surjection, bound Betti numbers by a multipartition filtration, identify the cocharacter-fixed scheme.
quote: Its two main comparisons have different purposes: a calculation for the full topological torus identifies the cohomology algebra, while a separate argument identifies that torus-fixed scheme with the fixed scheme of the stability cocharacter.

backbone: Build a fourfold from an arithmetic ball-quotient arrangement containing an abelian surface with infinite cyclic pi_1-image; hyperbolic path-graph readings verify infinite order and non-Stein cover.
quote: We construct a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover is not Stein.

backbone: Exhibit explicit algebra A; an exponentiated locally nilpotent derivation makes A[w] polynomial; a valuation degeneration and rigidity obstruction on derivations show A is not.
quote: We construct an explicit integral complex affine fourfold $X$ with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$ but $X\not\cong\mathbb A^4$.

backbone: Build a genus-21 curve with prescribed residue data, glue vector-field jets into an analytic contraction with free derivations, then algebraize by finite determinacy.
quote: We construct a singular normal affine complex surface whose tangent sheaf is free of rank two.

backbone: Exhibit an explicit degree-five polynomial via a hypersurface presentation that makes one-variable stabilization explicit; a graded/line-bundle obstruction shows a coordinate would force a derivation excluded by a rigidity argument.
quote: We construct an explicit degree-five polynomial over $\C$ that is not a coordinate in four variables but becomes one after adjoining a single variable.

backbone: Explicit rank-two bundle glued from two line bundles along three graphs; quotient sequences give ampleness; a positive metric would force an invariant measure with incompatible invariances.
quote: We construct $G$ together with two line-bundle quotients. Their dual inclusions will span away from three graphs and agree on those graphs through specified linear maps.

backbone: Extremal holomorphic discs and Hessian estimates give bounded canonical potentials, so K_X is nef; Aubin-Yau metrics with uniform volume give positive top self-intersection, so K_X is big, hence ample.
quote: Equation~\eqref{eq:intro-volume} gives a positive lower bound for their volumes. Passing to the limit in cohomology as $t\downarrow0$ proves $\int_X c_1(K_X)^n>0$.

backbone: Local product boxes adapted to both foliations are analytically continued by Hartogs-type extension across mixed boundaries; path rectangles assemble a biholomorphism of the universal cover onto a product.
quote: Our proof replaces these additional flatness or leaf hypotheses by extension estimates for maps adapted to the two distributions.

backbone: Define an explicit alternating product of corrected small diagonals; a formal detector functional kills Pixton's span but not the class, while Quot-scheme virtual localization proves the class vanishes in Chow.
quote: We construct a relation outside that system: an alternating product of corrected small diagonals that vanishes in rational Chow, and therefore in rational cohomology.

backbone: Assume a very general cubic of large discriminant rational; a divisorial birational cocycle with integral lattice cancellation forces a K3 from a bounded test collection, impossible for large d.
quote: Integral cancellation and the surface forced by rationality

backbone: Compute the unique Gepner eigencharge, build a two-parameter family of double-tilt aisles with uniform inclusion under the autoequivalence (using Xu's BG-type inequality), and refine to a slicing with support property.
quote: We construct such a condition for every smooth quintic threefold.

backbone: Low-discrepancy places stabilize and are extracted; a Shokurov-type difficulty (low places, flipped-surface cycle ranks) strictly descends along the flips, forcing termination; lc reduces to gklt.
quote: A decreasing sequence of subsets of a finite set stabilizes, which gives \eqref{eq:stable-low-places}.

backbone: On a maximal-Betti cover the Albanese fibre group N is FAb; if N were infinite, a minimal base and L2-Dolbeault/Hilbert-tensor arguments give a Bogomolov sheaf, contradicting specialness.
quote: It remains to exclude infinite \(N\); a finite kernel of a lattice quotient gives virtual abelianity by elementary group theory.

backbone: Rescaling a semialgebraic cover with recenterings and successive faces builds an intrinsic quotient; its deck action is discrete with symmetric base; fibres and affine factor assemble the product.
quote: In the present proof, the intrinsic quotient is constructed before its deck action is proved discrete and its base is identified as symmetric.

backbone: Chain-type weighted-homogeneous seeds of orders 2 and 3 with matching spectra; local-global arithmetic gives an integral Seifert isometry; open-book classification yields the ambient homeomorphism.
quote: We construct two reduced hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have multiplicities two and three.

backbone: Weighted Dolbeault index theory on the cyclic cover gives sections whose divisors have only compact components (cylinder estimates); counting b2 rational curves yields a global spherical shell.
quote: We construct divisors directly on the infinite cyclic cover of the given surface, and prove that every component is compact. The estimates must work for all the compact Chern classes needed in the eventual curve count.

backbone: Smooth contact-line pairs to very free conics, extend and descend moving-pair tensors to get contact transitivity, identify X with an adjoint variety, then pass via twistor spaces to Wolf spaces.
quote: The first-jet generation obtained below supplies such an immersion; we give the resulting contact moment-map classification directly.

backbone: Point-descendant lower bounds force algebraically independent eigenvalues of quantum divisor matrices, giving rho independent chained curve degrees; the ordered-chain method gives the bound, minimal families equality.
quote: Our argument first detects independent curve degrees in quantum correspondences. Proper covering families enter only at equality, when all the selected degrees are minimal.

backbone: A resolution invariant is shown constant via algebraic-curve reduction and semistable log models, giving a simultaneous resolution; continuous gradient lifts extend transport to ambient right-triviality.
quote: Our argument instead obtains transport from a resolved zero family and extends it to the ambient function levels.
